title: Question
description: One bank record: SPEC.md 3.1 (the question) and 3.2 (the verified record). Each $defs name is the dataclass of the same name in pipeline/src/popquiz/bank.py, and pipeline/tests/test_bank.py walks the two against each other in both directions so they cannot drift. This schema is the published contract; it is documentation plus that drift test, NOT a validator the pipeline runs — there is no JSON Schema validator in the Python standard library and pipeline/pyproject.toml is owned by another ticket. Records are validated by being loaded through bank.question_from_dict, which refuses unknown fields and enforces the structural rules. There is deliberately no `correct` property: SPEC 3.1 marks the correct answer derived (G-2), so it is computed by bank.correct_index and there is nowhere to write one down (AC-7).

id.description: Written by the generator, or by the organizer for a hand-written question.

source.description: The Rust program, within the room's fit bound (AC-100, SPEC 5.2).

difficulty_requested.description: What the run asked for. The organizer's judgement goes in review.difficulty_judged, and bank-audit fails a run on the drift between them (AC-88).

options.description: Exactly five, exactly one of kind does_not_compile, so its presence signals nothing (AC-24). THIS ORDER IS NOT THE WALL'S ORDER. Letters and the arrangement a room sees are drawn from the meetup date and nothing else (AC-23); bank order exists so two runs of a writer agree, and no reader may take a position tell from it (AC-26).

verified.description: Absent until the verifier has run. Written by the verifier and never edited.

used.description: One record per club that has run the question (D-26, AC-105). A bare object, which is what the bank wrote before clubs, is read as the default club's; the bank always writes a list.

why_tempting.description: The middle beat for this option: why a reader would pick it (D-9, AC-95). SPEC 3.1 files this under explains; it is carried on the option instead, a recorded deviation — see bank/README.md. Absent on the correct option, which has no tempting to explain, and absent while a question awaits its beats. Affirm is blocked until every incorrect option has one (SPEC 7.4).

takeaway.description: The third beat: what to remember. SPEC 3.1 names this field; the prototype's `argue` was a Stage-2 leak.

legacy.description: The MVP's single explanation string, kept verbatim so AC-73's quoted-output check runs against the text the organizer reviewed in August (SPEC 3.1). Never rewritten and never merged into the beats.

steps.description: May be empty. A question with fewer than two steps cannot be affirmed (SPEC 7.4), so an empty trace is the honest state for a walk-through nobody has written. For a question that ran, the last step is the one whose values names stdout (D-10).

lines.description: 1-based source lines drawn as executing now (SPEC 5.3).

focus.description: Inclusive 1-based [first, last] kept at full contrast; everything outside is dimmed.

note.description: The words the host reads for this step.

pivot.description: Marks the one step to pause on; the wall adds 'Pause here.' Optional in SPEC 5.3, so false is written as absence.

was.description: Verbatim; an em dash for absent.

Verified.description: SPEC 3.2. Three shapes are legitimate: complete and it ran; complete and it does not compile (no runs, no stdout, no exit_code, no miri — nothing ran, D-22); and legacy (D-16), which holds ONLY what the August MVP batch recorded. A field the verifier did not observe has no key at all — not a key holding null. For a legacy record that absence is the whole proof that nothing was back-filled (G-2).

rustc.description: The full `rustc -Vv` output for a complete record; for a legacy record the single-line `--version` string the MVP wrote, and never a -Vv reconstructed from it.

legacy.description: True on a record migrated from the August batch (D-16). False is written as absence, so the exceptional case is the one that shows in a diff. A legacy record renders the same step list as a complete one (SPEC 7.5, D-25), is exempt from the stale-pin check (SPEC 7.2), and is replaced whole — never merged — when T-15b re-verifies its question.

target_triple.description: Absent on a legacy record, where take-it-home reads 'not recorded' (AC-87). Never inferred from the machine that happens to be running.

stdout.description: What the program printed, written by the verifier and never by a person (AC-7, PHILOSOPHY 3). May be empty: a question whose answer is a panic printed nothing. The correct option is the one whose text equals this, normalized by the one trailing newline println! added.

compile_error_code.description: Every code the compiler reported, present only when the answer is 'does not compile' (AC-11). T-14 renamed the MVP's error_codes to this; the codes are the compiler's, unchanged.

byte_identical.description: Whether all runs produced byte-identical output. Evidence of determinism, not a guarantee of it (PHILOSOPHY 4).

Flags.description: The flags the research found unpinned (AC-6).

Miri.description: Miri proves absence of undefined behaviour ON THE PATHS ACTUALLY EXECUTED and nothing wider (AC-43, PHILOSOPHY 4). version, configs and seeds are absent on a legacy record, whose pass ran outside the verifier and recorded none of them (D-16).

clean.description: False is not a failure: it is how a record states that undefined behaviour is the declared answer (AC-9).

output_matched.description: Whether Miri's output matched the native output (AC-10). The receipt's Miri line renders only when this is true.

configs.description: The borrow models run. AC-9 accepts UB as an answer only when Stacked Borrows and Tree Borrows agree.

Review.description: Written by the review surface (SPEC 7.4). An absent status means nobody has judged this question yet, which is not rejection.

reason.description: Required when rejecting, and readable by the generator's next run (AC-19).

affirmed_by.description: Affirmation is separate from acceptance and blocking: no question reaches a deck without it (AC-72, G-12). Who and when are both recorded, so one without the other is not affirmed.

near_duplicate_of.description: Set by dedupe when a candidate is above the similarity threshold but below exact; it lands in the review queue, neither accepted nor dropped (AC-16).

Used.description: Written by the release transition and nothing else (G-10). NOT by a deck build: build_deck.py wrote a ledger line at build time, which retired questions for meetups that then did not happen, and that is a retired defect (BUILDPLAN 2).

club.description: The club whose room released the question (D-26); absent reads as the default club, nyc. A question is never run twice for one club; another club may still run it.

fit.description: The wall's measured verdict at reveal, the last refit of the night (AC-100). Absent when the wall never reported a verdict before release: the room sends null, and absent is absent (F-30). Absent is not fits.
